parsed.explanation: The combined regime has two layers that diverge sharply. The state/province is genuinely protective: public-accommodation and hate-crime law covering gender identity, trans-panic defence abolished, X markers on state IDs and birth certificates, a 2023 care shield law, and a 'Most Protective' tier placement — so everyday exposure inside the state is low (severity 1–2). But the federal layer governs the stages every visitor must pass: the Feb 2025 entry cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, permits fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, and several governments issued travel advisories over identity-document rules. Federal buildings carry facility bans; federal immigration and corrections custody document forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse and conversion-therapy-style treatment of trans detainees. A traveller's worst credible outcome is administrative refusal or custody harm, not imprisonment for identity itself, but the federal exposures are universal or state-run, and remedies are in active litigation.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse cases where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, and to weigh fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; X-marker passports no longer issued; multiple governments issued advisories to trans travellers. Applies at every crossing.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires all four elements, has limited waivers and is never automatic; challenges pending in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening is federal and cannot be offset by the state's protective ID regime; a state X licence may itself become 'evidence casting doubt' at federal inspection.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. One documented restroom arrest nationally (24h in men's ward).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State hate-crime enhancements and abolition of trans-panic defences; state sits in the 'Most Protective' tier; no state-specific custody abuse documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest or immigration hold moves the traveller from the protective state system into federal custody, where the hostile policy operates.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; facility bans in many states, 4 with criminal triggers. National facilities inside the state follow federal rules.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The state has no mapped facility ban, sits in the top protective tier, and its 2007 equality law covers public accommodations and public services uniformly across the state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State law protects private and state venues; federal building exclusion persists regardless, and national maps note other defining-sex policies may still apply.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders and proposed rules target gender-affirming care; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records nationally in 2025; funding freezes and loan-forgiveness blocks.
care_services.protection: State shield law (2023) protects patients and providers from civil or criminal charges when care legal here was banned at home; state public coverage and conversion-therapy ban for minors documented.
care_services.interaction: Shield law covers out-of-state charges but not federal DOJ process; narrowed upper-chamber text leaves some covered categories unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders, 'gender ideology' framing, counterterrorism strategy naming 'radically pro-transgender' groups, and a directive to criminally prosecute those facilitating a minor's social transition establish official hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State equality law, 2019 mental-health de-stigmatisation statute, and protected schools policy upheld through 2020; several federal orders blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal education department is actively investigating this state over trans athletes, pressuring state institutions the visitor may use.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order criminalising facilitation of a minor's social transition, under-19 record subpoenas, and Oct 2025 proposed public-insurance bar create risk for a travelling family seeking care or school-adjacent services.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law, conversion-therapy ban (2015), inclusive schools policy upheld on appeal, and anti-bullying law covering harassment.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent seeking care for a minor sits at the intersection of a protective state provider and federal investigative authority.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National 2025 poll: 66% support sex-at-birth document rules; national hate-crime bias data shows persistent anti-LGBT bias incidents; only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-motivated-violence statutes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute adds punishment for gender-identity bias; 2007 public-accommodation law; trans-panic defences abolished 2022; no state-specific violence or police-abuse incidents documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State recourse exists but charging and prosecution statistics for gender-identity hate crimes in the state are not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: National posture is contested and shifting; passport suit, executive orders and health rules unresolved, so exposure varies by travel date. No state data on police stops, custody treatment, airport screening, or enforcement of the accommodations law against excluding venues.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on passport/ID rules; active civil-liberties litigation; functioning state equality commission framework; courts have repeatedly upheld state protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation cuts both ways — some orders blocked, but the Supreme Court allowed the passport restriction to take effect.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-B there is routine state-run identity scrutiny with weak real-time remedies, and the federal custody record is worse than anchor harassment. But the anchor's exposure is a standing street-level police practice reaching daily life; here screening is confined to federal entry and federal buildings, while the state's daily sphere is protective. Higher than 0.35-B.

Closest match: extended secondary screening on document divergence, discretionary refusal, administrative rather than criminal penalty, appeals slow and rarely revised, high uncertainty from officer judgment. Our dossier adds documented federal custody abuse and official hostility (pulling down) but a strongly protective state environment for the stay itself (pulling up). Roughly level.

0.75-C has border officers trained to respect trans documents, tribunal review, and compensation for unlawful holding. Here the official instruction runs the opposite way — refuse on sex doubt, consider lifetime ineligibility — and several governments issued advisories. State-level protections are comparable to the anchor's, but the entry stage is materially worse, so lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences one country with two regimes. Everything inside the state's own sphere — hotels, restaurants, state offices, clinics, public spaces — is governed by a long-standing, uniformly applied equality law plus hate-crime enhancement and a care shield law, giving low everyday severity. Everything at the boundary and in federal custody is governed by a deliberately hostile national regime: sex-doubt refusals, fraud-based ineligibility, X-marker withdrawal, federal facility exclusion, and documented abuse of trans federal detainees. Because entry screening is unavoidable and custody, once triggered, is severe, the score cannot reach the Reduced-Risk band despite the state's protective tier; because the daily-stay exposure is mild and recourse exists, it sits above the 0.35 anchors. For an adult with a minor, the federal under-19 record subpoenas and social-transition prosecution order add a distinct, unresolved risk layer the state shield law only partly answers.
